summary.text: 友 is written as two 又 hand forms. Early descriptions associate them with friendship; some analyses also give 又 a sound role. The graph is used for “friend,” though the earliest reported contexts include a personal name and a sacrificial use.

formation.text: The graph is best described as a disputed semantic or phono-semantic compound: two 又 forms are read as hands and linked to friendliness, while another account assigns 又 a phonetic role as well. The evidence does not settle whether one or both forms supply sound, or how each contributes.

components.text: 又 is a pictograph of a hand. In 友, two such forms are described as facing the same way and sometimes joined; this supports a two-hands analysis, but not certainty about the intended scene. Some accounts treat both as semantic; another also assigns a phonetic role, whose exact placement is unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: The reconstructed comparison makes a sound role plausible but does not establish whether one or both 又 forms are phonetic. Current Mandarin readings alone do not demonstrate the ancient relation.

sound.text: In Mandarin, 又 and 友 have similar readings, but this modern resemblance alone does not prove the ancient sound role.
In Middle Chinese, the supplied reconstructions give similar syllables with different tone categories.

In Baxter–Sagart’s Old Chinese reconstruction, the forms share their initial and most of their rhyme material but differ in the final element, making a phonetic connection plausible without proving the role.
In Zhengzhang’s reconstruction, 又 and 友 likewise share initial and medial/rime material but differ in the final element.

history.text: Reported oracle-bone forms, bronze forms, Chu manuscripts, and small-seal forms show the graph across several stages. The early two-hand arrangement is described as having the forms oriented alike, sometimes joined; the small-seal forms arrange them vertically. These reports do not establish a specific historical image or concept of cooperation.

The received Shuowen account explains 友 through two 又 forms and associates it with people who share aims and interact as friends. This is a historical interpretation of the graph, not independent proof of its original intended meaning.

uncertainties.text: The dossier reports different emphases: two 又 as semantic hand forms, and 又 as both semantic and phonetic. The sound comparison supports a possible phonetic contribution, but does not resolve which repeated form has which role.

The reported earliest contexts are an oracle-bone personal name and a sacrificial use read as 侑; the available evidence does not establish “friend” as the earliest attested sense or give a continuous path from those contexts to later friend and associate uses. The cited witnesses were not independently inspected here.

A reported Mawangdui manuscript writes 柔 (“soft”) with 友. This is a separate reported use of the whole graph for another word; the evidence here does not independently verify the sound basis for that loan.

senses.period: oracle-bone context; absolute dating of the cited witness unresolved
senses.text: The earliest reported contexts include use of the graph as a personal name; this attestation does not establish the character’s original meaning.

senses.period: oracle-bone context; absolute dating of the cited witness unresolved
senses.text: The graph is also reported in an oracle-bone sacrificial context, read as 侑, “assist in sacrifice.” Its priority relative to the personal-name use is not established.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze contexts reported; individual witness dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze inscriptions are reported using 友 for friend or friendly relations and for associates. These attestations do not by themselves establish a semantic development from the earlier reported name or sacrificial use.
A dictionary records a verbal use meaning to make friends or become acquainted, but its example does not establish when this use arose.
A dictionary lists “love” among the character’s uses; the supplied evidence gives no chronology or supported link to other senses.
A dictionary lists assistance or cooperation as a use, without evidence here for its chronology or semantic connection to the other senses.
The character is currently used with the sense “friend” or “companion.”

limitations.text: The sources attest several uses but do not establish a chronological or semantic bridge among the early name, sacrificial, friend, associate, verbal, and other dictionary-listed uses; no development links are asserted.

The reported 友-for-柔 manuscript spelling concerns borrowing the graph for another word, not a demonstrated development in the meaning of 友. The underlying sound comparison is not independently established in the supplied evidence.

overview.text: 友 is written with two hand forms (又), associated with friendship. The character means “friend” or “companion”; accounts differ on whether the hand forms also cue its sound.

components.text: 又 depicts a hand. Two such forms are linked with friendship; the evidence leaves their exact sound role unsettled.

relationships.text: The two 又 forms are interpreted as hands contributing the idea of friendship, though the intended scene is not certain.
Each 又 is described as a hand form; the reported graph brings two such forms together. This describes the component imagery, without asserting a literal scene of cooperation.
One account explicitly assigns 又 a sound role, and Old Chinese comparisons show close forms with a differing final element. The evidence does not settle whether one or both 又 forms supply sound.
